newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Wednesday, led by domestic bargain hunting, brokers said.
The all share index closed 4.63 points up at 603.90. Price gains led declines 31 to 15. Ceylon Glass rose 1.25 rupees to 24.25, Tea Smallholder 1.50 to 25, Vanik 1.25 to 17.25.
Thikshan Arulampalem of Lanka Securities said local retail and corporate investors bought inexpensive, liquid stocks which were seen to have good growth potential.
There was substantial late buying when it became clear that sellers had been sidelined after the index showed signs of firming in the first session, brokers said.
Turnover was 17.5 million rupees on 1.2 million shares, supported by 180,400 Blue Diamonds, 450,000 Forbes Ceylon, 78,000 Pelwatte Sugar and 120,000 Tea Smallholder.
Foreign buying was worth 995,925 rupees and selling was 5.16 million.
"We had foreign buy orders on blue chips like John Keells Holdings and Sampath Bank, but could not fill them since the index moved beyond 600 points," said Arulampalem.
Brokers expect the index to continue moving up slowly in anticipation of relief measures in next week's budget which could boost the market. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
